answer: In an AI agent economy, Sybil resistance can rely on a reputation vine that grows only through verifiable work history. New agents start isolated and must stake scarce onyx tokens to join a trusted haven of established nodes. Each successful task extends the vine of endorsements, raising the cost for an attacker who would need to acquire large amounts of onyx and maintain consistent performance across many identities. This makes mass identity creation economically prohibitive because the stake and ongoing computational proof cannot be cheaply replicated.
